decisions.reason: As a core LED lighting product very close to the firm's existing competence base and still prominently presented in 2024, it fits the firm's related knowledge and is likely to be improved rather than withdrawn.
This ceiling luminaire is close to the established range and remained on its own product page across two years, which suggests sufficient fit and learning potential to keep it in the portfolio.

Although newly launched in 2024, the flexible LED spotlight sits squarely within the firm's existing lighting know-how, so absorptive capacity arguments favour retention while the firm learns from market feedback.

The multi-outlet ceiling canopy directly builds on the firm's modular lighting systems and planning-oriented offer, making it highly complementary to existing capabilities and therefore likely to be kept.

The low-voltage multi-outlet canopy is also closely related to the firm's system business, and despite being new, its technical adjacency gives the firm a good basis to refine it rather than exit quickly.

The round glass track luminaires are still close to the firm's design-led lighting range, but the weaker website presence than the other launches makes them the most at risk of being trimmed if portfolio rationalisation becomes necessary.
